title: The $41 night shift
scenario: A company runs two agents. Agent A updates dependencies every night on the Claude Agent SDK. Agent B triages support tickets on the OpenAI Agents SDK. Both had a bad week. You read the configs and the incident notes (exhibit).
exhibit:
AGENT A  deps-updater  (Claude Agent SDK, nightly CI job)
  options:  no max_turns, no max_budget_usd
  app code: on each ResultMessage -> post message.result to Slack

  2026-09-30  subtype: success
              result: "All dependencies updated."
              next morning: 3 test files fail on main
  2026-10-03  ran 3 h 12 min, total_cost_usd: 41.80

AGENT B  triage  (OpenAI Agents SDK)
  Runner.run(triage_agent, ticket_text, max_turns=6)

  2026-10-02  MaxTurnsExceeded raised
              -> customer saw: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error

questions.prompt: Which change puts a hard cap on what one run of Agent A can spend?

options.text: Set `effort` to `"low"` for the whole session.
options.explanation: Lower effort uses fewer tokens per turn, so it reduces cost. It does not stop a run at any amount.
Right. When spend reaches the cap, the SDK stops and returns subtype `error_max_budget_usd`. Subagent spend counts too.

options.text: Add "keep the cost under $5" to the prompt.
options.explanation: A prompt line asks the model; it does not stop the run. The SDK option stops the run at the cap.

options.text: Rely on automatic compaction to keep the context small.
options.explanation: Compaction keeps a long run going. It does not end the run, so it is not a spend cap.

questions.prompt: After adding the budget, some nights the Slack post is empty or the job crashes. Why?

options.text: The budget cap deletes the session, so no message is sent.
options.explanation: Every result subtype still carries cost, usage and the session id. Only the `result` text is missing.

options.text: The SDK raises an exception at the budget cap, so the app never gets a `ResultMessage`.
options.explanation: At the cap the SDK first yields a normal `ResultMessage` with subtype `error_max_budget_usd`. A single-shot `query()` raises only after that message. The message arrives, but without a `result` field.

options.text: `result` exists only on `success`; the app must check `subtype` first.
options.explanation: Right. On `error_max_budget_usd` there is no `result` field. The Claude docs say to always check the subtype before reading it.

options.text: A budget stop returns subtype `success` with an empty result.
options.explanation: A budget stop has its own subtype, `error_max_budget_usd`. That is how the app can tell it apart.

questions.prompt: For Agent B, the team wants a polite fallback reply instead of an HTTP 500 when the turn limit hits. What fits the OpenAI Agents SDK docs?

options.text: Pass `error_handlers` with a `"max_turns"` handler that returns a fallback output.
options.explanation: Right. The runner accepts `error_handlers` keyed by error kind, so it can return a controlled final output instead of ending with the error.

options.text: Set `max_turns=None` so the exception can never happen.
options.explanation: That removes the safety stop. A ticket that sends the agent in circles would then run with no turn limit.

options.text: Catch the exception and run the same input again with the same limit and the same tools.
options.explanation: The same input with the same limit can hit the same limit again, and the customer still waits for nothing.
That changes when every run ends: the first tool output becomes the answer. It is not a fallback for the turn limit.

questions.prompt: On 2026-09-30, Agent A said it was done, but tests failed. Which change targets that failure?

options.text: Raise `max_budget_usd` so the agent has more room to finish.
options.explanation: That run ended with `success`, not at a limit. More budget does not make it check its work.

options.text: Lower `max_turns` so the agent spends less time on each night of work and stops sooner.
options.explanation: A lower limit stops runs sooner. The problem was a run that stopped too soon already.

options.text: Set `stop_hook_active` to false in the options.
options.explanation: `stop_hook_active` is an input that a Stop hook receives, not an option you set. It is true when Claude is already continuing because of a stop hook.

options.text: Add a `Stop` hook that returns `decision: "block"` until the tests pass.
options.explanation: Right. A Stop hook block prevents Claude from stopping and gives it the reason, such as: run the test suite before finishing.
